package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of jQuery allow prototype pollution via the extend() API, enabling attackers to inject properties into the Object prototype. This can lead to privilege escalation, denial of service, or arbitrary code path manipulation in applications using jQuery for deep object merging with untrusted input.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
let a = $.extend(true, {}, JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {"devMode": true}}'));
console.log({}.devMode); // true
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code merges a user-controlled object containing a __proto__ property into a new object using jQuery.extend(true, ...), causing the devMode property to be set on Object.prototype, which is then accessible globally.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows user input to modify the global Object prototype, which can affect all objects in the application and lead to privilege escalation or logic manipulation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, deep merging should only affect the target object, not the global prototype chain. Here, untrusted input is able to pollute the prototype.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deep merging of configuration objects is common, but should not allow prototype chain modification.
key_indicators: Use of __proto__ property in user input
Recursive merge without prototype property filtering

execution_context.file_location: application code using jQuery.extend() with user input

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code parses a user-controlled JSON string containing a __proto__ property and deep merges it into a new object, resulting in the isAdmin property being set on Object.prototype and accessible from all objects.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input is used to set properties on the global prototype, which can be exploited to escalate privileges or bypass security checks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Application expects only the cloned object to be affected, not the global prototype chain.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deep cloning of user data is common, but should not allow prototype pollution.
key_indicators: Deep merge without prototype property filtering
Privilege escalation via polluted prototype (e.g., user.isAdmin === true)

execution_context.file_location: application code using square bracket notation

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code directly assigns a property to the Object prototype via myObj['__proto__']['a'] = 'a', causing all new objects to inherit the property a with value 'a'.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly modifying the prototype chain via user input or unguarded code can have global, unintended side effects.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal object property assignment should not affect all objects globally.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely legitimate; prototype modification is almost always a code smell.
key_indicators: Global property leakage to all objects

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes a list of package objects, one of which has a __proto__ key. When merged into packagesMap, this pollutes Object.prototype with a toString property, affecting all objects globally.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User-controlled data is used as object keys without filtering, allowing prototype pollution and global method override.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Mapping user data should not affect the global object prototype.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Mapping package data is common, but should not allow prototype chain modification.

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits user-controlled JSON or object containing a __proto__ property.
attack_chain.leads_to: Application processes the input using unsafe deep merge or mapping.

attack_chain.action: Application merges or assigns the user input into an object using jQuery.extend() or direct assignment, without filtering prototype keys.
attack_chain.leads_to: The Object prototype is polluted with attacker-controlled properties.

attack_chain.action: Subsequent code accesses properties (e.g., isAdmin, toString) on objects, which now resolve to attacker-controlled values via the prototype chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation, logic manipulation, or denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: Deep merge (e.g., jQuery.extend(true, ...)) of user-controlled objects containing __proto__, constructor, or prototype keys
Assignment to object properties using user-controlled keys without filtering
Unexpected global properties appearing on Object.prototype (e.g., isAdmin, toString)
file_indicators: Use of jQuery.extend(true, ...) with untrusted input
Direct assignment to ["__proto__"] or ["constructor"] in application code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for deep merge or object assignment operations where user-controlled data is used as keys, especially if the keys are __proto__, prototype, or constructor. Audit code for use of jQuery.extend(true, ...) or similar recursive merge utilities with untrusted input. Use static analysis to flag assignments to __proto__ or suspicious object key usage. At runtime, detect unexpected properties on Object.prototype or global objects.
